label: produces
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a chemical entity: asserts that the activity or state of the subject brings the object into existence.
observations: Causal-graph counterpart of METPO:2000202, which inherits rdfs:domain METPO:1000525 (microbe) via METPO:2000001 and so cannot be satisfied by any CausalNodeTypeEnum subject (TraitMech#301). Paired positive of METPO:2007801. Edges whose subject IS an activity (BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS, PATHWAY, MOLECULAR_FUNCTION) are NOT migrated here - they take RO:0002234 (has output), whose domain 'biological process or activity' they satisfy; this term is for the protein, trait and chemical subjects that RO cannot cover.

label: does not produce
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a chemical entity: asserts that the subject, under the stated conditions, does not bring the object into existence.
observations: Paired negative of METPO:2007800, following the kg-microbe paired-predicate convention. Mirrors METPO:2000222 with a causal-node domain.

label: reduces
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a chemical entity: asserts that the subject donates electrons to the object, lowering its oxidation state.
observations: Causal-graph counterpart of METPO:2000017 (TraitMech#301). Kept distinct from oxidizes/hydrolyzes rather than collapsed into a single catalytic relation: collapsing role-bearing predicates is what lost the donor/acceptor distinction in TraitMech#303. NOTE the corpus writes two senses under the label 'reduces' - this redox sense, and a 'lessens/decreases' sense on about 11 edges that this definition does not cover. Those need relabelling onto RO:0002212 before the term's usage matches its definition; tracked in TraitMech#330. The exemplar cited here is deliberately a redox edge.

label: oxidizes
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a chemical entity: asserts that the subject removes electrons from the object, raising its oxidation state.
observations: Causal-graph counterpart of METPO:2000016 (TraitMech#301). Sister of METPO:2007802.

label: exports
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a chemical entity: asserts that the subject moves the object from the cytoplasm across a membrane to the cell exterior.
observations: Causal-graph counterpart of METPO:2000209 (TraitMech#301). RO models transport at the process level, so there is no RO relation whose domain admits the GENE_OR_PROTEIN subject these edges use - which is why METPO:2000208/2000209 carry no RO xref upstream either.

label: imports
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a chemical entity: asserts that the subject moves the object from the cell exterior across a membrane into the cytoplasm.
observations: Causal-graph counterpart of METPO:2000208 (TraitMech#301). Sister of METPO:2007804; see that row on why RO offers no substitute.

label: has carbon source
definition: A relation between a trait and a chemical entity: asserts that the object supplies the cell carbon that the subject trait's metabolism assimilates.
observations: Role-bearing trait -> chemical relation in the same shape as METPO:2007701/2007702 (has electron donor/acceptor, TraitMech v8). Relabelled from METPO:2000006 'uses as carbon source' because the subject is the trait rather than the organism that uses it.

label: has energy source
definition: A relation between a trait and a chemical entity or environmental factor: asserts that the object supplies the free energy the subject trait's metabolism conserves.
observations: Sister of METPO:2007806. Range is deliberately wider than chemical: 6 of the 8 corpus edges point at an ENVIRONMENTAL_FACTOR (light), which is an energy source but not a chemical entity.

label: hydrolyzes
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a chemical entity: asserts that the subject cleaves the object by the addition of water.
observations: Causal-graph counterpart of METPO:2000013 (TraitMech#301). Scoped to the 6 edges LABELLED 'hydrolyzes', in which the subject is the hydrolysing agent. A 7th corpus edge shares the CURIE METPO:2000013 under the label 'is hydrolyzed to' (cellulose -> cellobiose, both CHEMICAL) and reads in the inverse direction, substrate to product; migrating it here as-is would assert that cellulose hydrolyses cellobiose. It is deliberately NOT counted and needs its own decision first (TraitMech#327).

label: degrades
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a chemical entity or cellular structure: asserts that the subject breaks the object down into simpler constituents.
observations: Causal-graph counterpart of METPO:2000007 (TraitMech#301). Range admits CELLULAR_LOCALIZATION as well as CHEMICAL: 1 of the 6 corpus edges degrades a plant cell wall.

label: accumulates
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a chemical entity: asserts that the subject causes the object to build up to an elevated intracellular concentration.

label: disproportionates
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a chemical entity: asserts that the subject splits the object into a more oxidized and a more reduced product.
observations: Causal-graph counterpart of METPO:2000200 (TraitMech#301). Distinct from METPO:2007603 (serves as electron donor and acceptor, TraitMech v6), which relates the chemical to the process rather than naming the splitting action.

label: transports
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a chemical entity: asserts that the subject moves the object across a membrane without committing to direction.
observations: Causal-graph counterpart of METPO:2000207 (TraitMech#301). Direction-neutral parent sense of METPO:2007804/2007805; retained because the single corpus edge does not specify a direction.
